strings.name: Jeff Dean
strings.role: Computer scientist; Discovery Loop cofounder and CEO
strings.summary: Jeff Dean helped build Google's search, distributed systems and machine-learning infrastructure. With Sanjay Ghemawat and other collaborators, he advanced MapReduce, Bigtable and TensorFlow, shaping large-scale computing and AI engineering. He became Google's chief scientist in 2023, then left in 2026 to cofound Discovery Loop with three longtime collaborators to automate research experiments.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributes to Google's distributed-computing and machine-learning infrastructure, advancing large-scale data processing and artificial-intelligence engineering.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor's in computer science and economics, University of Minnesota; computer-science PhD, University of Washington
strings.highlights.h1.title: Foundations for computing at scale
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Ghemawat and others, he developed MapReduce and Bigtable to simplify massive data processing and distributed storage.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From ML systems to research automation
strings.highlights.h2.text: He contributed to TensorFlow and later cofounded Discovery Loop; automating research is its goal, rather than an already achieved general capability.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Founding Discovery Loop
strings.timeline.t1.text: He left Google and cofounded the public benefit corporation with Ghemawat, Quoc Le and Oriol Vinyals, becoming CEO and initially targeting automated ML experiments.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Google chief scientist
strings.timeline.t2.text: As Brain and DeepMind merged, he took responsibility for AI technical direction and strategic projects across both research organizations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: TensorFlow open-sourced
strings.timeline.t3.text: The machine-learning system he helped build became publicly available, enabling researchers and developers to share working tools.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Bigtable paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: With the team, he described a distributed storage system for large-scale structured data.
strings.timeline.t5.title: MapReduce paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Ghemawat, he introduced a programming model and implementation simplifying parallel cluster data processing.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining Google
strings.timeline.t6.text: He worked on search and early advertising systems, then helped build infrastructure supporting the company's growth.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Computer-science doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: At Washington, supervised by Craig Chambers, he studied whole-program optimization for object-oriented languages.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Minnesota undergraduate degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He earned a degree in computer science and economics and had already explored neural networks as an undergraduate.
